title: DeploymentOpsContract
description: Machine-readable deployment entrypoint contract: OpenTofu owns infra state, root Makefile owns operator entry, day-2 changes route through ops, and infra/onprem shell is legacy inventory to migrate into Rust where appropriate.

source_directives: For deployment, no handrolling everything done with opentofu and minimal and intuitive boostrap, install, Makefile.
once setup everything should be managed through ops.
no manual ssh command troubleshooting. just works out of the box.
currently too many shell scripts. consolidate what we can do rust where it make sense to do so.

deployment_authority.rationale: OpenTofu declarative state is the only normal path for provisioning, resizing, DNS/tunnel/access, alerts, and deployment infra drift correction.

roots.state_policy: root-declared backend; do not hand-edit provider state; do not mutate OCI resources with oci CLI or console outside audited break-glass
root-declared backend; tunnel, DNS, and Zero Trust Access are OpenTofu-managed

makefile.command_policy: Make targets may invoke cargo/Rust gates and tofu only. They must not embed ssh troubleshooting, oci compute mutation, terraform CLI, or per-component infra/onprem shell scripts.

bootstrap_contract.goal: Cold-start the deployment toolchain without bespoke runbooks.
minimum_behaviour: validate this deployment contract with Rust
verify tofu is installed and point to official OpenTofu install docs if absent
run tofu init for infra/oci and infra/cloudflare
avoid networked package installation except OpenTofu/provider downloads requested by tofu init
non_goals: run component shell install scripts directly

normal_flow: leave day-2 host/service changes to ops-managed controllers
install_contract.confirmation_policy: OpenTofu apply prompts by default; do not use hidden auto-approve in the Makefile.

ops_management_contract.rule: After bootstrap/install, desired-state changes, drift repair, status, and incident workflows are initiated through ops or repo-native Rust controllers, not ad hoc SSH sessions.
incident_flow: route fix through CI/CD hotfix PR or OpenTofu desired-state change
do not page a human and do not manually SSH-troubleshoot

preconditions: active production safety incident where OpenTofu/ops is unavailable
audit-chain row emitted before or immediately after action
follow-up PR restores declarative desired state
break_glass.normal_runbook: not present; break-glass is not a troubleshooting recipe

shell_consolidation.policy: Rust owns idempotent host/component orchestration where logic branches, status checks, dependency ordering, rollback, or diagnostics exist. Shell may remain only as a cold-start shim that immediately execs Rust/OpenTofu, or as temporary legacy inventory until replaced.

completed_consolidation.rule: No hand-written phase logic, manual action recipes, OpenTofu apply snippets, or component shell dispatch may remain in this top-level file.
Diagnostics entry is Rust-owned and reports deployment-contract/shim health without SSH troubleshooting.
Destructive teardown is routed to Rust/ops planning instead of direct shell execution.
The retry loop is Rust-owned and invokes OpenTofu directly; shell may only locate the repo and exec the Rust command.
OCI readiness probes are Rust-owned read-only command executions with evidence output; shell must not embed probe logic.
On-prem bring-up routes through Makefile bootstrap/install plus OpenTofu and ops; shell must not run sudo package/service installation recipes.

migration_order.reason: replace top-level shell orchestration with Rust CLI entrypoints

acceptance_criteria.rule: root Makefile exists and exposes all required targets
OpenTofu roots are the only deploy mutation authority for OCI and Cloudflare
manual SSH troubleshooting and OCI CLI mutation are explicitly forbidden
every infra/onprem shell script is inventoried for Rust migration, with top-level setup/diagnose/uninstall orchestration already shimmed to Rust
the deployment durable goal no longer routes incidents to page-on-call
root deployment helper scripts are compatibility shims that exec Rust ops commands

verification_commands: cargo run -p oya-dev-cli -- gate validate deployment-ops-contract
